title: Impact of Close-Election Incumbency on Reelection Probability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Why: Incumbents who barely win versus barely lose are plausibly comparable except for treatment assignment (winning). The running variable is the incumbent’s vote-share margin around the cutoff of 0. Treatment switches discontinuously at 0 (win if margin ≥ 0). Estimating the jump in reelection probability at that cutoff identifies the local average causal effect of barely winning the prior election on the probability of winning reelection.

Key assumptions:
- Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of reelection probability varies smoothly with the vote-share margin at 0.
- No precise manipulation of the running variable around the cutoff (no bunching exactly at 0).
- SUTVA and accurate measurement of the running variable and outcome.

We implement a local linear RDD with a triangular kernel at the cutoff and conduct robustness checks:
- Bandwidth sensitivity (narrower and wider h).
- Parametric polynomial specification with interactions.
- Donut RDD excluding observations extremely close to the cutoff.
- Placebo cutoff test.
- Cross-check that treatment assignment aligns with the sign of the margin.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# 1) Setup --------------------------------------------------------------------
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Try to load robust SE packages (optional); proceed if unavailable
have_sandwich <- requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)
have_lmtest   <- requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)

# 2) Read data ----------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s88_data.csv"
dat  <- read.csv(path)

# Check required columns
required_cols <- c("running_var", "treated", "y")
stopifnot(all(required_cols %in% names(dat)))

# Core variables
x <- as.numeric(dat$running_var)
y <- as.numeric(dat$y)

# Derive treatment from the running variable (for RDD consistency)
D_from_x <- as.integer(x >= 0)

# Compare provided treatment vs. sign-implied treatment
if ("treated" %in% names(dat)) {
  D_provided <- as.integer(dat$treated)
  mismatch_rate <- mean(D_provided != D_from_x, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Share of cases where provided 'treated' != I(running_var >= 0): %.3f\n", mismatch_rate))
}

# Basic sanity check for support on both sides of cutoff
has_below <- any(x < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
has_above <- any(x >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
if (!has_below | !has_above) {
  stop("Running variable does not have support on both sides of the cutoff. RDD is not feasible.")
}

# 3) Local linear RDD function -------------------------------------------------
llr_rdd <- function(y, x, h, donut = 0) {
  # y: outcome
  # x: running variable centered at cutoff 0
  # h: bandwidth
  # donut: exclude observations with |x| <= donut (0 => none)
  stopifnot(h > 0)
  keep <- !is.na(y) & !is.na(x) & (abs(x) <= h)
  if (donut > 0) keep <- keep & (abs(x) > donut)
  if (sum(keep) < 20) return(list(est = NA, se = NA, pval = NA, n = sum(keep), h = h, donut = donut))
  yk <- y[keep]
  xk <- x[keep]
  Dk <- as.integer(xk >= 0)
  wk <- pmax(1 - abs(xk)/h, 0)  # Triangular kernel weights

  df <- data.frame(y = yk, x = xk, D = Dk, w = wk)
  fit <- lm(y ~ D + x + D:x, data = df, weights = w)

  # Extract coefficient on D (the discontinuity at the cutoff)
  coef_idx <- which(names(coef(fit)) == "D")
  if (length(coef_idx) == 0) return(list(est = NA, se = NA, pval = NA, n = length(yk), h = h, donut = donut))

  est <- coef(fit)[coef_idx]

  # Robust standard error if possible
  if (have_sandwich && have_lmtest) {
    vc  <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
    ct  <- lmtest::coeftest(fit, vc)
    se  <- as.numeric(ct["D", "Std. Error"])
    pvl <- as.numeric(ct["D", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  } else {
    sm  <- summary(fit)
    se  <- sm$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"]
    pvl <- sm$coefficients["D", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  }

  list(est = as.numeric(est), se = as.numeric(se), pval = as.numeric(pvl),
       n = sum(keep), h = h, donut = donut)
}

# 4) Main estimate and bandwidth choices --------------------------------------
max_abs_x <- max(abs(x), na.rm = TRUE)
# Default bandwidth at 20% of support; plus narrower and wider alternatives
h_main <- 0.20 * max_abs_x
h_alt1 <- 0.10 * max_abs_x
h_alt2 <- 0.30 * max_abs_x

main_est <- llr_rdd(y, x, h = h_main)
alt1_est <- llr_rdd(y, x, h = h_alt1)
alt2_est <- llr_rdd(y, x, h = h_alt2)

cat("\nMain local-linear RDD (triangular kernel) at cutoff 0\n")
cat(sprintf("Bandwidth h = %.4f | N used = %d\n", main_est$h, main_est$n))
cat(sprintf("Estimated discontinuity (win effect on reelection prob): %.4f\n", main_est$est))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n", main_est$se, main_est$pval))

cat("\nBandwidth sensitivity:\n")
cat(sprintf("h = %.4f | N = %d | Effect = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f\n",
            alt1_est$h, alt1_est$n, alt1_est$est, alt1_est$se, alt1_est$pval))
cat(sprintf("h = %.4f | N = %d | Effect = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f\n",
            alt2_est$h, alt2_est$n, alt2_est$est, alt2_est$se, alt2_est$pval))

# 5) Donut RDD robustness ------------------------------------------------------
donut_radius <- 0.02 * max_abs_x
donut_est <- llr_rdd(y, x, h = h_main, donut = donut_radius)
cat("\nDonut RDD (excluding |x| <=", sprintf("%.4f", donut_radius), "):\n", sep = " ")
cat(sprintf("h = %.4f | N = %d | Effect = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f\n",
            donut_est$h, donut_est$n, donut_est$est, donut_est$se, donut_est$pval))

# 6) Parametric polynomial RDD (with interactions) -----------------------------
# Use a moderate window for parametric fit
win_poly <- 0.30 * max_abs_x
keep_poly <- abs(x) <= win_poly
Df <- as.integer(x >= 0)

if (sum(keep_poly, na.rm = TRUE) >= 30) {
  df_poly <- data.frame(y = y[keep_poly], x = x[keep_poly], D = Df[keep_poly])
  fit_poly2 <- lm(y ~ D + x + I(x^2) + D:x + D:I(x^2), data = df_poly)
  if (have_sandwich && have_lmtest) {
    vc_poly2 <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit_poly2, type = "HC1")
    ct_poly2 <- lmtest::coeftest(fit_poly2, vc_poly2)
    est_poly2 <- as.numeric(ct_poly2["D", "Estimate"])
    se_poly2  <- as.numeric(ct_poly2["D", "Std. Error"])
    p_poly2   <- as.numeric(ct_poly2["D", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  } else {
    sm_poly2 <- summary(fit_poly2)
    est_poly2 <- sm_poly2$coefficients["D", "Estimate"]
    se_poly2  <- sm_poly2$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"]
    p_poly2   <- sm_poly2$coefficients["D", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  }
  cat("\nParametric polynomial RDD (quadratic with interactions) within |x| <=", sprintf("%.4f", win_poly), ":\n", sep = " ")
  cat(sprintf("Effect (coef on D): %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f | N = %d\n",
              est_poly2, se_poly2, p_poly2, sum(keep_poly)))
} else {
  cat("\nParametric polynomial RDD skipped (insufficient data in window).\n")
}

# 7) Local randomization check: near_cutoff subsample --------------------------
if ("near_cutoff" %in% names(dat)) {
  near_mask <- as.integer(dat$near_cutoff) == 1 & !is.na(y) & !is.na(x)
  if (sum(near_mask) >= 20) {
    df_nc <- data.frame(y = y[near_mask], x = x[near_mask], D = Df[near_mask])
    fit_nc <- lm(y ~ D + x, data = df_nc)  # small adjustment for x
    if (have_sandwich && have_lmtest) {
      vc_nc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit_nc, type = "HC1")
      ct_nc <- lmtest::coeftest(fit_nc, vc_nc)
      est_nc <- as.numeric(ct_nc["D", "Estimate"])
      se_nc  <- as.numeric(ct_nc["D", "Std. Error"])
      p_nc   <- as.numeric(ct_nc["D", "Pr(>|t|)"])
    } else {
      sm_nc <- summary(fit_nc)
      est_nc <- sm_nc$coefficients["D", "Estimate"]
      se_nc  <- sm_nc$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"]
      p_nc   <- sm_nc$coefficients["D", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    }
    cat("\nNear-cutoff subsample (local randomization) estimate:\n")
    cat(sprintf("Effect (coef on D): %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f | N = %d\n",
                est_nc, se_nc, p_nc, sum(near_mask)))
  } else {
    cat("\nNear-cutoff subsample estimate skipped (insufficient near_cutoff observations).\n")
  }
}

# 8) Placebo cutoff test -------------------------------------------------------
placebo_c <- 0.25 * max_abs_x
xp <- x - placebo_c
has_below_p <- any(xp < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
has_above_p <- any(xp >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
if (has_below_p && has_above_p) {
  plc_est <- llr_rdd(y, xp, h = h_main)
  cat("\nPlacebo cutoff test (cutoff =", sprintf("%.4f", placebo_c), "):\n", sep = " ")
  cat(sprintf("h = %.4f | N = %d | Placebo effect = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4f\n",
              plc_est$h, plc_est$n, plc_est$est, plc_est$se, plc_est$pval))
} else {
  cat("\nPlacebo cutoff test skipped (insufficient support around placebo cutoff).\n")
}

# 9) Final printout of the main causal estimate --------------------------------
cat("\n=== Final causal estimate (preferred) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Local-linear RDD at cutoff 0 with triangular kernel\n"))
cat(sprintf("Effect (win vs. lose at threshold) on reelection probability: %.4f\n", main_est$est))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error: %.4f | p-value: %.4f | Bandwidth: %.4f | N used: %d\n",
            main_est$se, main_est$pval, main_est$h, main_est$n))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Barely winning should increase the probability of reelection relative to barely losing, reflecting incumbency advantage from office-holding (name recognition, resources, fundraising).
- Magnitude: Typically 5–15 percentage points in close-election RDDs. I expect an effect around +0.08 to +0.12 on the reelection probability at the cutoff, with similar positive signs across bandwidths and robust to donut and parametric checks. Placebo effects should be near zero and statistically insignificant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze the discontinuity at the vote-share cutoff to isolate the effect of incumbency.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Winning a close election reduces the probability of reelection.
